paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures repeatedly use blue, orange/red, and green to distinguish initialization/method conditions; conceptual Figures 2–3 add colored state arrows; density Figures 1/4 use sequential fills. Colors are supplemented by line style, marker, panel position, and labels, but no single fixed semantic palette spans all objects.

paper_style.style_consistency: The two-column ICML layout, Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography, thin rules, and small serif plot labels are stable. figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. An overview of the impacts and performance of the proposed methods. (a) The default Kaiming initialization causes the signal diminishing problem, where the post-synaptic current variance (σ²) rapidly decreases across layers (l). (b) Our proposed ETTFS-init method regulates these distributions. (c) ETTFS-init accelerates convergence and improves accuracy, with performance further enhanced by weight normalization. (d) Our proposed decoder reduces the average inference time-steps compared to the previous TQ-TTFS decoder across four datasets.

encodings.y: density, accuracy, or average inference time-steps
encodings.text: μ, σ², l=0…4, panel labels, and local legends

figures.data_and_statistics: Panels (a,b) show five layer-wise distributions with μ and σ² annotations; (c) compares Kaiming init, ETTFS-init, and ETTFS-init+norm over epochs; (d) compares three decoder/method bars on MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR, and DVSGesture. The figure gives no replicate count or uncertainty.

design_strengths: A compact 2×2 map links mechanism, convergence, and deployment latency.
Panel (a,b) distribution annotations make variance shrinkage visible.
Method colors and local legends provide a quick entry to later tables/ablations.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Physical latency comparison between (a) layer-by-layer propagation and (b) step-by-step propagation in a three-layer SNN with T = 4 time-steps. Each layer consumes one time unit to process one time-step, and the output spike S^i[t] is transmitted immediately after it is generated, where i denotes the layer index and t denotes the time-step. In layer-by-layer propagation, each layer must wait for the complete input spike sequence before producing its own output sequence, which leads to latency accumulation with network depth. In step-by-step propagation, spikes are forwarded across layers at every time-step, which reduces physical latency.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. The neuronal dynamics of the AMOS neuron include three stages: charge, fire, and mask update. In the charge stage, the membrane potential H[t] accumulates via the input X[t]. During the fire stage, the neuron generates a spike S[t] = 1 if both the membrane potential H[t] surpasses the threshold Vth and the mask F[t − 1] is zero; otherwise, S[t] = 0. The mask F[t] is updated by accumulating S[t] at the mask update stage.

caption.text: Figure 5. (a) The mechanism of the temporal weighting decoder. (b) Comparison between average-pooling and max-pooling in TTFS SNNs.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 previews initialization, convergence, and inference cost; Figure 2 explains latency; Figure 3 gives the AMOS one-spike state chain; Figure 4 diagnoses WN distribution stability; Figure 5 explains TWD and pooling. Tables 1–3 carry accuracy, steps, and energy comparisons. Figures 6–9 and Table 4 provide gradient, depth, component, and gamma ablations; Appendix Tables 5–8 preserve sensitivity, coding, and architecture details.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use italic Figure/Table labels and sentence-case prose. Figures 1, 2, 4, and 6 state mechanism or directional findings; Figures 7 and 9 are short and rely on plot/section context. Tables define datasets, footnotes, and shorthand, but `±`, seeds, and most aggregation rules are not defined.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1 and 7 use two-level dataset→Model/Acc headers; Table 2 is method×dataset; Table 3 is metric/cost columns; Table 4 is component flags plus accuracy; Tables 5–6 are sensitivity grids; Table 8 is two repeated `# / Layer Description` blocks. Booktabs/no-vertical-rule styling is stable.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 2–5 are method-interface/mechanism diagrams; Tables 1–3 are main comparison and efficiency cost; Figures 6–9 and Table 4 are ablation/mechanism diagnostics. Appendix Tables 5–8 extend time-step/variance sensitivity, coding-form comparison, and architecture disclosure. No independent repeated component-deletion or significance analysis is provided.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figure 1(d) links to Table 2; Figure 2 to the latency discussion; Figures 3 and 5 to Eqs. (4–8) and (21–27); Figure 4 and Figure 8 to Table 4; Figures 6–7 to initialization/depth claims; Figure 9 to gamma tuning. Tables 1/7 link to Table 8 architecture expansion; Appendix Tables 5–6 hold T/variance scans.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern families dominate body, caption, table, and diagram math; Nimbus Mono appears in the PDF font inventory for code-like material. Thin rules and small labels recur across charts/tables, with local density driven by panel count and annotation count.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange/green recur for method conditions, while red, yellow, pink, and teal are task-specific. Markers/line styles are available in Figures 1, 2, 7–9, but density fills and colored arrows still depend on color for fast interpretation; citation blue in tables is text styling rather than data encoding.

most_reusable_patterns: 2×2 overview linking mechanism distributions to convergence and deployment metrics.
Two-slice propagation/state diagrams for timing and one-spike invariants.
Explicit component/sensitivity tables that expose the selected configuration and its alternatives.
Compact architecture grammar in a parallel `# / Layer Description` table.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: contribution overview across mechanism, training, and inference.
Table 1: broad benchmark comparison with model/condition annotations.
Tables 2–3: steps and multiple energy proxies.
